chunks: And whatever is in it from Ismaʿīl ibn Abī Fudayk, I have narrated it from al-Ḥusayn ibn Aḥmad ibn Idrīs—may Allah be pleased with him—from his father, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, from Ismaʿīl ibn Abī Fudayk.

key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: may Allah be pleased with him; an honorific supplication for the narrator
key_terms.عَنْ أَبِيهِ: from his father; part of the immediate transmission link in the chain
key_terms.عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي فُدَيْكٍ: from Ismaʿīl ibn Abī Fudayk; the endpoint narrator whose transmission route is being clarified
key_terms.فَقَدْ رَوَيْتُهُ: I have narrated it; an explicit statement of transmission by the compiler

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Ismaʿīl ibn Abī Fudayk in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits narrations from Ismaʿīl ibn Abī Fudayk in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh. Its significance lies in documenting the chain of transmission for hadith preservation and source attribution.
